slides.headline: $1,100 IN FREE AI YOUR STUDENT ID ALREADY UNLOCKS

caption:
A student ID unlocks over $1,100 in free AI tools. Most students never claim them. 🤯

7 free AI tools your student card unlocks right now:

1) Google Gemini Pro
If your school runs on Google Workspace, Gemini is already sitting in your account. Most students never look. Sign in with your school email at gemini.google.com.

2) GitHub Copilot
The AI that writes code alongside you, inside your editor. Normally $10/month. Free through the GitHub Student Developer Pack. education.github.com. Use this one tonight.

3) AWS Educate
Amazon cloud credits, no credit card needed. Enough to build and deploy a real app for free. aws.amazon.com/education/awseducate.

4) Microsoft Azure $100
A hundred dollars in cloud credits, no credit card, no catch. Enough to run AI tools for months. It expires in a year, so actually use it. azure.microsoft.com/free/students.

5) Vercel Pro
Most devs deploy their first app here. Pro is $20/month; the GitHub Student Pack gives it to you free. Start at vercel.com.

6) Cursor Pro
Every developer you follow is switching to this editor. It's free if you have a .edu address. cursor.com/students.

7) Figma (the design app)
Every app you have ever used started as a Figma file. Normally $15/month. Free the moment your school email is verified. figma.com/education.

SAVE THIS: 7 tools your student ID already unlocks.

These are the same tools startups pay hundreds a month for. A school email is a key most students never use. If you know a student sitting on these, send this to them.

Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.

pinned_comment: Which one are you trying tonight? Number 2 is the move to start with. GitHub Copilot free for a year is worth more than most people's whole side hustle setup.

hook_tournament.why: $1,100 paired with YOUR makes you stop at 2am—it's so specific and personal you need to read the caption. [4] has the same compelling number but loses impact by addressing STUDENTS generically instead of YOU directly.
